solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Computer devices after backing up becoming smoother

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the word read here runs the other way

parts.note: taken as written, before it is turned round
a mouse is a computer pointing device

explanation.surface: Someone's computer equipment seems to run more smoothly once it has been backed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the computer devices second, behind the turned-round UP; 'backing up' looks like a data-saving phrase but splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light volcanic stone rubbed on skin or wood to abrade it, so it is literally a thing that makes surfaces smooth.

clue.text: One sharing job perhaps is to leave with watch

parts.note: to part is to go away or leave
a watch is a timer; 'with' just adds it

explanation.surface: A job-sharer may knock off early and keep an eye on the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a job-sharer is one kind of person working reduced hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people splitting one post each work only some of the week, which is exactly what a worker on reduced hours does.

clue.text: One starting a new life being married, I concede

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
to grant a point is to concede it, so 'I concede' is I GRANT

explanation.surface: Someone admits that getting married really is like starting life afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'starting a new life' mean marriage; it is really the definition, a person who moves to another country.
explanation.definitionFit: People who move abroad to settle are beginning afresh in a strange land, so this is a descriptive paraphrase of the noun.

clue.text: Mock royal receiving grand old man

indicators.note: whatever receives something takes it inside itself

parts.note: cod as an adjective means mock or sham, as in cod Latin
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A sham royal plays host to a distinguished elderly gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like an adjective for the old man, but it is the thousand-pound abbreviation, and 'mock royal' together forms the receiving pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Codger is an informal, affectionate word for an elderly fellow, often a slightly eccentric one.

clue.text: Shakespeare's first to reverence his justice

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the initial letter of the playwright's name
to hallow is to revere or treat as holy

explanation.surface: Revering Shakespeare comes first, as if it were the poet's due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakespeare's' does double duty: its first letter starts the answer and it supplies the 'his' of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Shallow is the foolish country Justice of the Peace in Henry IV Part 2 and The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: Rebuke son without emotion

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
someone cold shows no feeling

explanation.surface: A parent tells off their boy in a flat, unfeeling way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like a container or deletion signal, but here 'without emotion' is simply a phrase meaning unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to reprimand someone angrily for doing wrong.

clue.text: City article held back for broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so what counts is how the words are spoken

parts.note: the article is A, and held back is delayed

explanation.surface: A news item has been postponed before it goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a delayed' runs together into the name of the South Australian state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is a major Australian metropolis, capital of South Australia, so a straightforward example of a city.

clue.text: One king guarding another that is less discreet

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, keeping it inside

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's monarch
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: One monarch protects a second one who keeps fewer secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' looks like a link to the definition but supplies IE; LEAR holds both K and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A source that leaks more lets out more secrets, so it is less careful about confidential information.

clue.text: Accompanied by daughter to take inside measurement

indicators.note: taking something inside means wrapping around it

parts.note: with means accompanied by
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A tailor, with their daughter along, takes an inside leg measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside measurement' reads like a tailor's inside leg; 'inside' belongs to the container signal and 'measurement' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth from side to side is one of the standard dimensions measured of anything.

clue.text: Island, I gather, having many features

parts.note: the Isle of Man
taken as written
to gather cloth is to fold it into pleats

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that an island has plenty of attractions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gather' reads as 'I understand'; split it, and gather is a sewing term for folding fabric. The Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold as an adjective means of many kinds or aspects, varied and numerous.

clue.text: Equipment I had fixed

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone says the gear they owned has now been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' suggests mended; it is the definition in its sense of unbending.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigid is stiff and immovable, set firmly in place and unable to bend.

clue.text: Earlier, a shot in court

parts.note: taken as written
a forehand is a stroke on a tennis court

explanation.surface: A tennis rally earlier featured one fine stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot in court' could suggest a shooting at a trial; the court is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforehand is an old adverb meaning in advance or beforehand, at a previous time.

clue.text: Predictable blow, traffic having to twist and turn

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, often illicitly
a road that winds twists and turns

explanation.surface: Road traffic snaking along a twisty route delivers a foreseeable setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist and turn' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain synonym, and 'blow' looks like a setback but is a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds blow steadily from the same direction in the tropics, so sailors could rely on and forecast them.

clue.text: Like a chimp pair, regularly in tree

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Two chimpanzees sitting up a tree look just like chimps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair' suggests two; only its odd-numbered letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Apish means resembling an ape, and the chimpanzee is one of the great apes.

clue.text: Dull, short book, one of a collection

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its ending

parts.note: the first Gospel, one of the four in the New Testament

explanation.surface: A brief volume in a series is a boring read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of a collection' tells you the book is one of a set: the four Gospels. Its usual abbreviation drops the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A matt finish on paint or paper has no shine, so it is lacklustre and non-glossy.

clue.text: Thought blue team a different colour

parts.note: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservatives, CON for short
a side is a team
red is a colour other than blue

explanation.surface: Someone thought a team in blue ought to change its kit colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue stands for a Conservative, the UK party whose colour it is; 'a different colour' then contrasts with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have considered something is to have pondered it, so both are past forms of reflecting on a matter.

clue.text: Summer clothing small — take it off?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to undress is to take one's clothes off

explanation.surface: Skimpy summer clothes prompt a cheeky invitation to strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful 'take it off', a stripper's call, as a synonym for removing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless frock worn in hot weather is a typical item of warm-season attire.

clue.text: Protest against repeated cold snaps

indicators.note: something that snaps breaks, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: People complain about one cold spell after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold snaps' looks like a weather phrase, but 'cold' gives C and 'snaps' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate something is to express disapproval of it, which is a formal way of objecting.

clue.text: Complete confusion of business meeting swamped by papers

indicators.note: whatever is swamped is engulfed and surrounded

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is an annual general meeting of a company

explanation.surface: An annual meeting drowning in paperwork descends into total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swamped' nods to the literal meaning of the answer, a bog; an AGM is a company's annual general meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire figuratively is a messy, entangling situation from which it is hard to escape.

clue.text: Using drone in conflict is decisive

indicators.note: things in conflict clash and are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Deploying unmanned aircraft in a war proves the deciding factor.
explanation.walkthrough: The topical surface hides a ten-letter anagram of the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A resounding victory is emphatic and unmistakable, so the word means conclusive in that sense.

clue.text: Butterfly, one passing over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small, darting butterfly of the family Hesperiidae
second meaning: someone who skips, omitting or jumping over something

explanation.walkthrough: A butterfly flitting past makes 'passing over' seem physical; it means someone who leaves something out.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a family of quick-flying insects and also, literally, a person who skips pages or items.

clue.text: Hack work, first chapter

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter
OP, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A hack writer turns out the opening chapter of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' places the chapter before the work. 'Hack' suggests a writer for hire, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to cut roughly with heavy blows, just as one does with an axe or cleaver.

clue.text: Leader shortly taking band for audition

indicators.note: made short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a leader is a head, here cut short
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A bandleader soon brings his group along to try out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, matching 'audition'; it is a band of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An audition is literally a listening, and the word comes from the Latin for the act of perceiving sound.

clue.text: Disreputable and unsteady, speaking drunkenly

indicators.note: slurred speech changes how a word sounds, so we go by the drunk's pronunciation

parts.note: unsteady is loose, and a drunk slurs the s to sh

explanation.surface: A shady character, tottering on their feet and slurring their words.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is a slurred 'loose', which comes out sounding like the French-derived word for shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche describes someone of dubious morals, rakish and not quite respectable.

clue.text: Cargo in galleon's restricting progress

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the letters are held within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A heavy cargo slows a sailing ship's speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of 'Cargo', all of 'in' and the start of 'galleon's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Good going means good progress; the noun describes how fast one advances or the rate of advance.

clue.text: Old songs left for silly people mostly to collect

indicators.note: most but not all, so the final letter goes
collecting something means gathering it in and holding it

parts.note: geese are silly people; mostly loses the last letter
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Old songs abandoned for fools to gather up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned but is just L, collected by the shortened geese, an old insult for fools.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied part-song for three or more voices, popular in eighteenth-century England.

clue.text: Drink in fresh coffee at last, having done this?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: fresh as in cheeky is pert
cola is a fizzy drink

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fresh coffee is ready to drink once it has finished brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to the coffee: it is drinkable after it has filtered through. Read whole, the clue describes the process.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is made by letting hot water seep through grounds in a pot, and only then can it be drunk.

clue.text: Pressure on girl at last to consume tuck

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl is finally pressured into eating her snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for sweets and snacks, which steers the surface; here it is a fold sewn in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck and the answer are both folds stitched into fabric to shape a garment.

clue.text: Drained state of pint seems to require refreshing

indicators.note: refreshing something remakes it, so these letters are put together anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drained beer glass looks as though it needs a top-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refreshing' nods to buying another round, which is the surface joke; it signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass that has been drained has nothing left in it, so its condition is one of vacancy.

clue.text: Group of hotels, the third becoming the last in the country

indicators.note: the letter in third place leaves its spot and is moved to the end

parts.note: a hotel chain, with its third letter taken out
the letter removed from third place, now placed last

explanation.surface: A hotel chain's third property turns out to be the last one in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from a word for a group of hotels and move its third letter to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the large East Asian nation, so it is simply an example of a country.

clue.text: Being legless, repents moving about

indicators.note: letters moved about are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Having been legless (British slang for very drunk), someone is sorry as they stagger about.
explanation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for very drunk, which drives the surface; the definition means a creature with no legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake has no limbs, so a limbless creature is a fair description, and Eden's tempter was one.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about entertaining good music

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the word is read backwards
a host entertaining a guest has them inside

parts.note: eager means keen or enthusiastic
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A fan is keen on hosting some fine tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but turns the keen word round before it takes in G.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggae is the popular Jamaican genre with a strong offbeat rhythm, so it is an example of a musical style.
